about: Issue #4037 (slice 8a): the version 2 request the Core Updater writes on the update command's stdin and the result lines the Outpost apply writes on fd 3 (docs/misc/core-api-protocol.md, 'Update command, version 2'). Not used in production yet: Core's worker writes version 1 until #4038.

tests/php/CoreUpdateV2ContractTest.php runs every row against pfb_core_update_v2_request(), pfb_core_update_v2_alias() and pfb_core_update_v2_result(). #4038 runs the same file from Go when it writes the requests and reads the results: every accepted request must be one its request type writes or decodes, every result line one its reader parses with the same values, and no refused report may be a line it accepts.

A request row gives its stdin as 'request' (a JSON value, written as JSON) or as 'stdin': a string, or a list of parts joined in order, each a string or {repeat, times}: the string written times times, every '{i}' in it replaced by the repetition's index from 0.

A request row's verdict is 'accepted' (the normal form the validator returns), 'acceptedCounts' (the lengths of its lists, for a row too large to spell out) or 'refused' (the reason, word for word). A result row gives 'report' and either 'line', the exact bytes written, or 'refused'.

A result row gives its report as 'report' (a JSON value) or as 'reportJSON' (parts as a request row's 'stdin', joined and decoded), and its 'line' as a string or as such parts. A report names at most limits.ids ids across applied, removed and failed, each once, and at most limits.ids aliases in changedAliases, each once: as a request holds at most limits.ids ids across resources and removed, the report of every request accepted fits. No line is longer than limits.resultLineBytes, its newline included: when a report's line would be, every failure message longer than 'left out to fit the result line' becomes that text, and a report whose line is too long even then is refused.

Every field, written in one fixed order whatever the order given; generations are the strings the request gave.

An empty applied map or list says nothing and is left out; a false flag is kept.

A message of 1,024 bytes of non-ASCII text is cut to 1,024 bytes as escaped.

A quote that would end past the bound once escaped is left out whole.
A message cut where its escaped prefix is exactly 1,024 bytes: the emoji that ends at the bound, escaped as a surrogate pair of 12 bytes, is kept.
2,048 failures, each message 1,024 bytes of non-ASCII text: too long as one line, so every message is shortened.
